solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make good response to defeat — poh!?

parts.note: the clue word read in the opposite direction spells a jump, so it is a leap taken backwards: a spring term plus the word for rearwards

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disdain offered as the proper reaction to losing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poh' is HOP read backwards, i.e. a hop back; BOUNCE is another word for hop, so the clue word encodes BOUNCE BACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover quickly after a setback is the idiomatic way of responding well to a defeat.

clue.text: Agent providing security

definitions.meaning: James ... is the famous fictional secret agent 007
a certificate issued when borrowing money, a debt security

explanation.surface: A spy employed to keep things safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming's spy is the best-known agent; in finance the word names an interest-bearing security.

clue.text: Throw from Mount Everest's peak after wild onrush

indicators.note: after places the summit letter behind the rearranged letters
wild suggests the letters of onrush running out of control into a new order
the peak of a word is its top, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A climber is hurled off the summit of Everest after a violent surge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like part of the mountain name but is a noun meaning a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismount a rider forcibly is to throw them from their horse, the mount.

clue.text: Seethes about wife tucking into Fish Balls served up — they should be smoked

indicators.note: about means the agitated-water word goes round everything else

parts.note: seethes means churns, boils up

indicators.note: tucking into says the spouse letter goes inside the fish

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family

indicators.note: served up in a down clue reads the politician's name upwards

parts.note: Ed Balls is a British Labour politician, so Balls gives his first name

explanation.surface: Someone fumes while their wife tucks into fish balls.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls is a former UK cabinet minister; 'Fish Balls' reads as a dish but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: These are long-stemmed clay tobacco pipes, things one smokes.

clue.text: Auntie studied food workers provided

parts.note: Auntie, or the Beeb, is a nickname for the BBC
to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: An aunt revised what to cook for her staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The pollen and honey mixture is fed by worker bees to the larvae in a hive.

clue.text: Scene of gold rush includes gold material for necklace

indicators.note: includes says the state abbreviation holds the heraldic metal

parts.note: Cal is short for California, scene of the 1849 gold rush
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A prospecting site yields gold that might be strung into jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: The red or pink skeletons of marine polyps are polished and strung as beads.

clue.text: Spare list

definitions.meaning: spare in the sense of thin, with no fat
to list is to heel over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: An extra inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a spare figure is thin, and a listing ship tilts to one side.

clue.text: Engineering equipment in mill to fill with despair

parts.note: Eng is the usual abbreviation for engineering
a loom is the weaving machine found in a textile mill

explanation.surface: Mill machinery so oppressive it drives the workers to despair.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare verb meaning to make gloomy, to darken the mood.

clue.text: Where people go for holiday out of habit

definitions.text: Where people go for holiday out of habit

parts.words: Where people go for holiday out of habit
parts.note: out of habit reads as from routine, but means out of their clothing, a habit being a garment

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests creatures of routine returning to the same resort; the garment sense of habit turns it into undressed holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist resort is where people holiday without clothes.

clue.text: Returning from Jaipur he noticed a local statesman once

indicators.note: Returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Coming back from an Indian city, a traveller spots a former regional politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' ties the statesman to Jaipur, i.e. India.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister, a statesman of that country in the past.

clue.text: Listened in with attention like a judge

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention
British judges wear wigs, so a judge is bewigged

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdropped as closely as a judge hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is an informal British verb for eavesdropping on a conversation.

clue.text: Treatment for the very sick wounded veteran is nice

indicators.note: wounded suggests the words are damaged and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: An injured old soldier is a pleasant person who needs nursing.
explanation.definitionFit: The hospital unit giving constant close monitoring is where critically ill patients are treated.

clue.text: Harmony between ethnic groups could be upset by sectarian role

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters knocked over into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Community peace might be disturbed by a religious faction's part in things.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers how different ethnic communities get on; harmony is its ideal state.

clue.text: Simple meal — gotta piece cooking

indicators.note: cooking implies the letters are mixed up and transformed

explanation.surface: A casual cook says they must get a portion on the stove.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced beef topped with mashed potato is a plain, homely dish.

clue.text: Make threadbare outer garments?

definitions.meaning: to wear out a fabric until it is thin
whimsically, clothing worn over other clothing, by analogy with underwear

explanation.surface: Wearing coats until they are worn thin.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to wear out through use; split in two it pretends to be the opposite of underclothes.

clue.text: Coming out with pithy sayings

indicators.note: out suggests the word coming is put out of its normal order

explanation.surface: Someone emerges spouting aphorisms.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes speech or writing full of short, wise maxims.

clue.text: A poet's inspiration to take very little time

definitions.meaning: the Florentine woman Dante loved and wrote about
split as ..., to last only an instant

explanation.surface: A muse who works fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense works by reading the name in three words: BE A TRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's beloved inspired the Divine Comedy; a trice is a moment, so being one takes no time.

clue.text: Southwark hostelry where beer is served — get one small round

indicators.note: round says the small-amount word encircles the drinking counter

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
a bar is where drinks are served

explanation.surface: An old London inn invites you to buy a single small round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tabard in Southwark, south London, is where Chaucer's pilgrims gather; 'get one' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tabard was the Southwark inn from which the Canterbury Tales pilgrims set out.

clue.text: Stag sees first of blue-chips go up rapidly

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of blue-chips

parts.note: to rocket is to rise steeply, as prices do

explanation.surface: A stock-market bull sees leading shares soar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stag' looks like a market speculator in the share-trading scene; it is a deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brocket is a male red deer in its second year, a young stag.

clue.text: Want to be in the glow of old part of London

indicators.note: to be in says the desire word sits inside the glow word

parts.note: leam is an archaic word for a gleam or glow
to want is to wish for

explanation.surface: Longing to bask in the warmth of a bygone corner of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewisham is a borough of south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: The borough is a district of south-east London, so a part of the capital.

clue.text: Old Vietnamese leader's ready in India to give praise to the Lord

parts.note: Ho Chi Minh led North Vietnam; his name with the possessive s
ready is slang for cash, and an anna was a former Indian coin

explanation.surface: A communist leader is prepared, in India, to worship God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for money (ready cash), not prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew acclamation is a shout of adoration addressed to God.

clue.text: Travellers catch knaves about to strike up

indicators.note: about says the catching word goes round the striking word

parts.note: to get something is to catch it
to lob is to hit a ball high into the air
knaves and rotters are both scoundrels

explanation.surface: Arresting some villains who are on the point of going on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike up' looks like starting a tune; it is hitting upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: People who travel the world widely are travellers on a grand scale.

clue.text: Victorian novelist leaves his customer short

indicators.note: short says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a novelist's customer is someone who reads books

explanation.surface: A Victorian writer is abandoned by his patron who runs out of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade wrote The Cloister and the Hearth, a nineteenth-century English novel.

clue.text: Small amount of information in extra time

indicators.note: in places the time letter inside the cricket extra

parts.note: a bye is an extra in cricket, a run scored without the bat

explanation.surface: A little news arrives in added time at a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs not scored off the bat; a bye is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of computer data, usually eight bits, is a small quantity of information.

clue.text: Sort of Asian kept outside of India when English left

definitions.text: Sort of Asian kept outside of India when English left

indicators.note: sort of signals a rearrangement of the letters
left means the language letter has gone from the word kept

parts.note: India is I in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A national of the state kept separate from India after British rule ended in 1947.
explanation.walkthrough: In the all-in-one reading the clue describes Partition; 'outside of' only orders the pieces, which the shuffle makes irrelevant.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a citizen of the nation partitioned off from India when the British withdrew.

clue.text: Number beset by some bug

indicators.note: beset by says the number abbreviation is surrounded

parts.note: some and any are interchangeable determiners

explanation.surface: A figure surrounded by a few insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' is a verb meaning irritate, not an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is informally to irritate or pester them.

clue.text: 19th-century painter — not the first for modern art collector

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: J Paul Getty was an American oil billionaire and art collector

explanation.surface: An old artist is ignored in favour of a contemporary patron.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was an English painter of nudes active in the 1800s.

clue.text: Greek character denied turning base

indicators.note: turning says the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
reneged means went back on, denied a promise

explanation.surface: A Greek person refused to change their position.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the sense of morally low, corrupt or debased.
